newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Minister warns that Israel could oust Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Minister warns that Israel could oust Arafat.

text.p: Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi warned in remarks broadcast on Sunday that Israel could oust Palestinian President Yasser Arafat from the self-ruled Gaza Strip if violence erupted in the territories.
Hanegbi made the comment as Israel was set to begin as soon as Monday building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, a move the PLO has said could trigger widespread unrest.

"Whoever launches violence could very quickly find himself packing a suitcase and travelling back and forth on the line from Tunis to Baghdad like he (Arafat) did for many years," Hanegbi told supporters in the remarks on Saturday.
Hanegbi's counterpart in Arafat's Palestinian Authority, Freih Abu Medeen, cancelled a meeting with the Israeli minister following the speech.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said he regretted Hanegbi's remarks, telling Israel Radio: "They don't contribute to peace or security".

In the remarks Hanegbi said: "Arafat won't be able to sit in his villa on the beach with (his wife) Suha and give orders to act. There's no immunity for anyone wishing to annihilate us, neither for 'The Engineer' nor anyone in any villa.
"If war, then war to the end," he said.

"The Engineer" was the code name of the master bomber Yahya Ayyash, responsible for suicide attacks of the Islamic militant group Hamas that killed scores of Israelis. He was killed in January 1996 when a mobile phone exploded in what was widely seen as an Israeli assassination.
Arafat's aide Ahmed Tibi said Hanegbi's remarks had "caused an escalation".

"Hanegbi spoke in an immoral style and used base language to express his views," Abu Medeen, the Palestinian official in charge of justice, told Reuters. He cancelled a meeting with Hanegbi scheduled for Sunday.
Arafat set up his self-rule authority in Gaza in 1994 under a peace deal with Israel after running the PLO for years from Tunis.
Palestinians say Netanyahu's plans to build the settlement on land occupied by Israel in 1967 have caused a crisis in peace moves with the Jewish state.
